answers.stem_only: Use server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C): the company sends its own key over HTTPS with each PUT and GET; S3 encrypts and decrypts the object but does not store the key (only a salted HMAC to validate it). Client-side encryption fails the 'S3 itself must encrypt' requirement, and SSE-KMS or SSE-S3 keep keys in AWS. Make sure the bucket does not block SSE-C requests.

One lifecycle rule: keep in S3 Standard for 30 days, transition to S3 Standard-IA at day 30 (millisecond access, infrequent reads, multi-AZ because it is the only copy, objects above the 128 KB billing minimum), transition to S3 Glacier Deep Archive at day 90 (lowest cost, retrieval within hours fits the 24-hour wait, 7 years exceeds the 180-day minimum), and expire the objects after 7 years.
